name: Naturalization (2026 Rules)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 8 years of continuous habitual residence in Sweden (increased from 5 years under rules effective 6 June 2026). Absences over 6 total weeks in a year are subtracted from the qualifying period entirely.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 8 years of continuous habitual residence.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants aged 18-67 must show regular employment/self-employment income of at least SEK 250,200/year (approx. SEK 20,850/month before tax); more than 6 months of social assistance in the preceding 3 years disqualifies. Exemptions apply for pensioners, people with permanent disabilities, and full-time university students with satisfactory grades.
Applicants aged 16-66 must demonstrate Swedish at CEFR B1 (reading/listening) and A2 (speaking/writing), via approved school grades or the Tisus test.
requirements.fix_path: Pass the required Swedish language assessment.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires demonstrated knowledge of Swedish society (via social-studies grades, or the new citizenship test on Swedish society, available from August 2026; a Swedish-language citizenship test follows no earlier than autumn 2027).

Must have lived, and be expected to continue living, 'an orderly and honourable life'. Unpaid debts generally require a 2-year wait after payment; criminal convictions carry qualifying waiting periods from 2 years (day fines) up to 17+ years (lengthy prison sentences).
Citizens of Denmark, Finland, Iceland, or Norway need only 2 years of residence, and may use a simplified notification procedure rather than a full application.

Spouses/registered partners/cohabitants of a Swedish citizen need 7 years of residence (up from 3 years pre-June-2026), including at least 5 years living together, plus the income and language/civics requirements applicable to the standard route.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 7 years of residence, including 5 years living with the Swedish-citizen spouse/partner.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants under 21 need 7 years of residence.
Stateless persons need 5 years of residence (up from 4 years pre-June-2026).
Recognized refugees need 7 years of residence (up from 4 years pre-June-2026).

evidence_required.document: Proof of residence period matching the applicable category
Swedish language and civics test results or qualifying school grades

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: Absences totaling more than 6 weeks in a year during the qualifying period are subtracted entirely from the residence count.

sources.title: Swedish Migration Agency -- Apply for Swedish citizenship (current rules, post-6-June-2026 reform): 8-year standard residence, income floor SEK 250,200/year, B1/A2 language levels, civics test, good-conduct standard, category-specific reduced periods

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sweden). MAJOR RECENT REFORM, worth flagging prominently: these rules took effect 6 June 2026 -- less than 3 months before this research pass -- and represent, per Migrationsverket's own comparison, 'the most significant citizenship requirements overhaul' in the law's history: standard residence 5->8 years, spouse/cohabitant track 3->7 years, refugee track 4->7 years, stateless track 4->5 years, plus an entirely NEW income/self-sufficiency requirement and NEW language/civics tests (civics test live from August 2026, language test not before autumn 2027 -- meaning the language-test COMPONENT of this requirement is not yet actually testable as of this file's verified_at date, a genuine implementation gap worth flagging). Persons who applied under the OLD (pre-6-June-2026) rules may still be processed under those terms depending on transition provisions -- not modeled here since this file reflects current-applicant rules only. See se_permanent_residence.json for the July 2026 change to how asylum-category applicants reach citizenship without a permanent residence permit (a 'well-founded prospects of renewal' test, or an automatic waiver after 10 years' residence).
